newsitem.title: USA: Defense asks court to throw out Abu-Jamal case.
newsitem.headline: Defense asks court to throw out Abu-Jamal case.

text.p: Lawyers for death-row author Mumia Abu-Jamal said on Friday they asked the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to rescind his conviction of the 1982 murder of a Philadelphia policeman and to bar the state from a retrial.

In filing an appeal with the Court, chief defence counsel Leonard Weinglass cited a federal judge's ruling that prison authorities had violated Abu-Jamal's rights by examining his correspondence with his lawyers.
"The waters are just too polluted for the case to carry on," Weinglass said at a press conference outside City Hall.

He said hearings this summer before Judge Albert Sabo on a new trial developed enough new evidence for the justices to reverse Sabo's decision in October denying the appeal. Weinglass also said Sabo's refusal to hear from 25 defence witnesses was grounds for appeal.
On Dec. 4, U.S. District Judge Donetta Ambrose, sitting in Pittsburgh, ruled that Abu-Jamal was constitutionally entitled to confidential communications with his defence lawyers.

Abu-Jamal was a black activist and radio journalist in 1981 when, according to police, he encountered his brother in a dispute with a white policeman issuing a ticket for driving his cab the wrong way on a one-way street. Abu-Jamal was convicted of shooting officer Dan Faulkner, whose return fire struck him in the chest.
While on death row Abu-Jamal wrote a book, "Live from Death Row", which won him celebrity backing and demonstrations on his behalf in Europe.

In Pennsylvania, Abu-Jamal is in a legal limbo. Judge Sabo has indefinitely postponed an execution warrant, originally dated Aug. 17, 1995. A state Supreme Court decision is not expected until late spring.
